newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Central Bank audits banks currency book.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Central Bank audits banks currency book.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank is looking at the foreign currency positions of banks to ensure they stay within prudent levels, an official said on Monday.
"It's a continuing special verification authority to check on the reports of overbought and oversold (dollar positions)," Central bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes told Reuters.
He said this was a regular weekly audit by the Central Bank and was not necessarily in response to last week's run on the peso.
The peso had been hit after the de facto devaluation of the Thai baht over a week ago.
Banks are allowed to be short or long on dollars up to a certain extent of their capital.
Reyes said the verification would also mean checks on whether banks were selling dollars without proper documentation.
Central Bank rules do not allow an outflow of dollars if there are no proper documents to show the investor had previously placed the same amount of dollars in the country.
